merger_description:
Imagine Education Early Learning Centres No. 40 Pty Ltd (**Imagine Education**) proposes to acquire the childcare centre business known as Bumper Bears Early Learning Centre (**Bumper Bears**) and a lease of the childcare centre from which the business operates from the existing owners. Children First Property Pty Ltd as trustee for the Children First Property Trust (**Children First**) proposes to acquire the land on which Bumper Bears operates.

Imagine Education and Children First are both part of the Imagine Education Group. The Imagine Education Group currently operates 63 childcare centres in Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia and Tasmania under the Imagine Childcare, Children First, Grow Early Education and Learning Ladder brands. Children First currently owns the land on which 6 Imagine Education Group centres operate.

Bumper Bears is run by a partnership between six members of the Sourris family. It operates a single childcare centre, Bumper Bears, which is located at 401 Elizabeth Avenue, Kippa-Ring QLD 4021.

The Imagine Education Group and Bumper Bears both provide centre-based childcare and early childhood education services (including long day care) for children up to 6 years of age.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is limited geographic overlap between Imagine
Education and Bumper Bears in the supply of centre-based
childcare and early childhood education services in Kippa-
Ring and the surrounding areas
b. there are alternative suppliers of centre-based childcare and
early childhood education services in Kippa-Ring and the
surrounding areas.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
